\section[bocciare]{bocciare — to fail (a student); to reject}

\label{lesson:IT-C383-bocciare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the notes, then the Italian for the textbook.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: bocciare}
\textbf{bocciare} — \textquotedblleft{}to fail (a student); to reject\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se non studi, ti bocciano.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you do not study, they will fail you.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Essere bocciato} — to fail a year or an exam. Of a plan: \emph{il progetto è stato bocciato}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bocciare} is built on \emph{boccia} \textquotedblleft{}a ball for bowls\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): first to knock away another player's ball, then to knock out a student. The origin of \emph{boccia} itself is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bocciare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bocciare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the notes, then the Italian for the textbook, then say \emph{bocciare} again
\end{itemize}

\section[la bocciatura]{la bocciatura — the failing (of a year or an exam)}

\label{lesson:IT-C383-bocciatura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the textbook, then the Italian for to fail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la bocciatura}
\textbf{la bocciatura} — \textquotedblleft{}the failing (of a year or an exam)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo la bocciatura ha cambiato scuola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After failing the year he changed school.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{bocciare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bocciatura} is built on \emph{bocciare} \textquotedblleft{}to fail (a student)\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{boccia} \textquotedblleft{}a ball for bowls\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); the origin of \emph{boccia} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[promuovere]{promuovere — to pass (a student); to promote}

\label{lesson:IT-C383-promuovere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to fail, then the Italian for the failing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: promuovere}
\textbf{promuovere} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass (a student); to promote\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se mi promuovono, a settembre vado in quinta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If they pass me, in September I go into the final year.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{muovere}; past participle \emph{promosso}. Also to promote a product or a person.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{promuovere} comes from Latin \emph{prōmovēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move forward, to advance\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{prō} \textquotedblleft{}forward\textquotedblright{} and \emph{movēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la valutazione]{la valutazione — the assessment, the evaluation}

\label{lesson:IT-C383-valutazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the failing, then the Italian for to pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la valutazione}
\textbf{la valutazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the assessment, the evaluation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La valutazione finale dipende anche dai compiti a casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The final assessment also depends on the homework.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{valutare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{valutazione} is built on \emph{valutare} \textquotedblleft{}to assess\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{valuta} \textquotedblleft{}value\textquotedblright{} and \emph{valere} \textquotedblleft{}to be worth\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, to be worth\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[il punteggio]{il punteggio — the score}

\label{lesson:IT-C383-punteggio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to pass, then the Italian for the assessment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il punteggio}
\textbf{il punteggio} — \textquotedblleft{}the score\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con questo punteggio entri all'università.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With this score you get into university.}
\end{quote}

In games and sport too: \emph{il punteggio finale}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{punteggio} is built on \emph{punto} \textquotedblleft{}point\textquotedblright{} with the ending \emph{-eggio}; \emph{punto} is inherited from Latin \emph{punctum} \textquotedblleft{}a prick, a point\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
